Understanding Cache Revalidation

HTTP caching lets clients reuse previously fetched responses instead of downloading them again. When a cached response expires, the client does not need to throw it away. Instead, it can ask the origin server whether the stored copy is still valid.

Conditional requests carry validators such as ETag and Last-Modified headers. If the resource has not changed, the server answers with a 304 Not Modified status and an empty body, saving bandwidth and time. If the resource has changed, the server sends the fresh representation with a 200 status as usual.

This handshake is cheap for both sides and is the backbone of efficient content delivery on the web. ArticleBodyMarkerText.
